items.title: The registration chain check tests a proxy, not the property
items.hypothesis: 'last-touching commit == pinned SHA' is red on an intact repository whenever history is merged from a line duplicating a registration commit, and green on a tampering that preserves commit identity. The substantive property -- pinned commit is an ancestor of the published branch AND the blob at HEAD equals the blob at the pin -- passes 4/4 today.
items.discriminatingTest: Replace the check; assert it stays green across the present duplicate history and goes red on a synthetic content change at HEAD with the pin untouched.
items.whyItMatters: A control that is permanently red teaches everyone to ignore it, and this one is red on a repository whose registrations verify.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether the chain alert is actionable at all.

items.title: Two gaps in the public-boundary check (PBC-101)
items.hypothesis: The local-path rule misses 11 of 37 real leaked lines (any path preceded by '=' or ':'), and 'lockpick' -- the one term the owner named as never-public -- is not on the internal-wording blocklist.
items.discriminatingTest: Replay the 37 removed lines; require 37/37 blocked. Assert the internal-tooling term is blocked.
items.whyItMatters: The highest-frequency leak shape in the repository is the one that slips through.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether the boundary check can be relied on for the class it claims to cover.
items.safety: owner judgement needed: the blocklist is public and names what it protects

items.title: Withheld-set checker for live commissions (M27 enforcement)
items.hypothesis: Publishing a run report can retire a live commission's pass condition. LIVE-COMMISSIONS.json declares the withheld sets; nothing enforces them.
items.discriminatingTest: Block additions containing any live commission's withheld values; verify it would have flagged the RUN-20260807-10 publication.
items.whyItMatters: M27 is currently prose, and this program's own rule (M26) is that prose is not a control.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether the next commission is issued blind or spoiled in advance.

items.title: LIN-000's registration under-determines its own pass condition
items.hypothesis: BL-044 measured 96 exhaustive orderings and 72 draw-schedule readings admitted by the registered prose, exactly one correct each. Fixes: define the generator in-document (counter-based), register draws as primitives not distributions, specify boundary cases and enumeration orders, and publish prefix digests.
items.discriminatingTest: Re-commission against a revised registration; a second implementation should hit both digests on its pre-declared reading, with no sweep.
items.whyItMatters: Answers whether the F11 repair generalises. Today it does not: it buys 'one coin-flip away', not a stream.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether KL-000 adopts schedule registration program-wide (BL-016/F11).
